section_summary: This section concerns diplomatic representations and technical evaluations by the Department of State, the Federal Communications Commission, and the Navy Department regarding radio interference caused by Japanese stations and vessels between late 1939 and early 1940. Major issues include interference by Japanese stations JZI, JDK, and JND with American broadcasts from KGEI, Press Wireless station KJY, and Naval Radio Station NSS, as well as Japanese ships interfering with naval direction-finding off California. It also contains detailed reports from Batavia on Far Eastern shortwave reception conditions and concludes with an unrelated 1932 telegram concerning emergency communications in China.

subfiles.about: Concludes Ambassador Grew's report on reprimanding Commercial Attaché Williams regarding Mrs. Williams' indiscreet communication to the Treasure Island radio station.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports cautioning Commercial Attaché Williams against further indiscreet communications by his wife to the Treasure Island radio station.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ambassador Grew regarding Mrs. Williams' Communication to Treasure Island Radio Station

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Ambassador Grew's report regarding the reprimand of Commercial Attaché Williams concerning Mrs. Williams' letter to Station W6XBE.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: The Department acknowledges Grew's report that he notified Commercial Attaché Williams of its attitude regarding Mrs. Williams' letter to Station W6XBE.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Ambassador Grew regarding Mrs. Williams and Station W6XBE
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits an Embassy memorandum delivered to the Japanese Foreign Ministry protesting interference by station JZI with broadcasts from American station KGEI.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits an Embassy memorandum delivered to the Japanese Foreign Ministry providing FCC data on interference by Japanese station JZI with American station KGEI.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4245 from Tokyo regarding Interference by Japanese Station JZI with Station KGEI

subfiles.about: Presents FCC monitoring data showing station JZI operating off-frequency and causing heterodyne interference with KGEI.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Presents FCC measurements showing Japanese station JZI operating below its assigned frequency, causing heterodyne interference with station KGEI, and requests corrective action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from American Embassy, Tokyo to Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Reports that the Embassy is continuing to press Japanese authorities for a reply concerning radio interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the Embassy continues pressing Japanese authorities for an answer regarding radio interference and expects a reply soon.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 683 from Tokyo regarding Radio Interference Negotiations

subfiles.about: Notes that further action is apparently needed regarding radio interference.
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Brief internal note stating that further action is apparently needed on the radio interference matter.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from Francis de Wolf to Harvey B. Otterman
subfiles.to: Harvey B. Otterman, Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: Transmits a complaint from Press Wireless, Inc. regarding continued harmonic interference from Japanese station JDK to station KJY.
subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Chairman Fly transmits a Press Wireless complaint regarding unabated second harmonic interference from Japanese station JDK to American station KJY.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly to Secretary of State regarding Station JDK Interference

subfiles.about: Reports severe and unabated second harmonic interference from station JDK in Dairen to Press Wireless station KJY in Daly City.
subfiles.from: D. K. de Neuf, Superintendent of Operations, Press Wireless, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Press Wireless reports severe second harmonic interference from Japanese station JDK in Dairen affecting reception of KJY in Manila and Shanghai, violating Cairo regulations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Press Wireless, Inc. to FCC regarding Second Harmonic Interference from Station JDK

subfiles.about: Instructs the Embassy to protest severe second harmonic interference by Japanese station JDK with station KJY in the Far East.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Instructs the Embassy in Tokyo to urge Japanese authorities to immediately eliminate harmonic interference from station JDK affecting station KJY in Manila and Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2 to American Embassy, Tokyo regarding Station JDK Interference

subfiles.about: Informs the FCC that the Embassy in Tokyo has been instructed to urge Japanese authorities to eliminate interference from station JDK.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith informs Chairman Fly that the Tokyo Embassy was telegraphed to urge Japanese authorities to eliminate station JDK's interference with station KJY.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly regarding Station JDK
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Discusses the deterioration of KGEI shortwave news reception in Java due to Japanese and European station interference and suggests frequency changes.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, American Consul General, Batavia, Java
subfiles.summary: Consul General Dickover details severe interference drowning out KGEI news broadcasts in Java from Japanese, European, and regional stations, suggesting a shift to 9603 kilocycles.
subfiles.title: Letter from Consul General Dickover to General Electric Company regarding Reception of KGEI in Java
subfiles.to: E. S. Darlington, Manager, Short-Wave Broadcasting, General Electric Company

subfiles.about: Requisition slip requesting one photostat copy of the KGEI dial settings chart.
subfiles.from: Division of International Communications, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Internal departmental slip requesting one photostat of the accompanying radio log chart.
subfiles.title: Photostat Requisition Slip from Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: Graphical dial-setting chart illustrating crowded shortwave frequencies and interference surrounding KGEI in Java.
subfiles.from: Dr. A. H. Hamilton, American Consulate General, Batavia
subfiles.summary: Radio dial chart illustrating crowded shortwave stations around KGEI's frequency and suggesting an alternative operating channel.
subfiles.title: Chart of Log Settings on 'Microlog' Radio Receiver by Dr. A. H. Hamilton

subfiles.about: Transmits Consul General Dickover's letter and chart regarding KGEI interference to the FCC for upcoming engineering discussions.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Long transmits Consul General Dickover's letter and frequency chart to the FCC for upcoming conferences with General Electric engineers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly Transmitting Batavia Consulate Report
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Requests diplomatic representations to Japan regarding excessive signal width and interference from station JND to Naval Radio Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Navy (Charles Edison / C. W. Nimitz)
subfiles.summary: The Navy Department requests representations to Japan regarding station JND's excessive signal emission width causing interference to Naval Radio Station NSS on 17.8 kilocycles.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department to Secretary of State regarding Interference by Station JND with Station NSS

subfiles.about: Instructs the Embassy to request Japanese authorities to correct station JND's emission bandwidth interfering with Naval Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull instructs the Tokyo Embassy to ask Japanese authorities to eliminate station JND's interference with U.S. Naval Radio Station NSS under Cairo regulations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6 to American Embassy, Tokyo regarding Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Informs the Navy Department that instructions are being sent to Tokyo regarding station JND's interference with station NSS.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith informs Edison that instructions are being dispatched to the Tokyo Embassy regarding interference caused by Japanese station JND to station NSS.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Acting Secretary of the Navy Edison
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Acting Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Requests representations to Japan regarding inter-ship radio traffic on 375 kilocycles by Eiyo Maru and Kaizyo Maru interfering with naval direction finding.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Navy (Charles Edison / C. W. Nimitz)
subfiles.summary: The Navy suggests diplomatic representations after Japanese vessels Eiyo Maru and Kaizyo Maru caused radio interference to naval direction-finding services off California on 375 kilocycles.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department to Secretary of State regarding Interference to Direction Finding by Japanese Vessels

subfiles.about: Confirms that the Embassy at Tokyo is being instructed to protest Japanese vessel interference with naval direction finding.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith informs Edison that the American Embassy at Tokyo is being instructed to request measures preventing Japanese vessels from interfering with naval direction finding.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy Edison
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador Grew to request Japanese authorities to prevent recurrence of interference to naval direction finding by Japanese vessels.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Navy's complaint and instructs Ambassador Grew to urge Japanese authorities to prevent future interference by Japanese vessels with naval direction-finding frequencies.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1877 to Ambassador Grew regarding Interference by Japanese Vessels
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Recommends not pursuing the direction-finding interference case further due to its isolated nature and more pressing radio negotiations.
subfiles.from: Harvey B. Otterman, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Otterman reviews the lack of further complaints regarding Japanese ship interference on 375 kilocycles and recommends dropping the matter to focus on pressing KGEI negotiations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Harvey B. Otterman to Thomas Burke on Closing Case of Japanese Vessel Interference
subfiles.to: Thomas Burke, Chief, Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: Reports that the American Minister to China will assist Page's representative with Chinese National Government authorities at Nanking regarding communications.
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Secretary Stimson advises F. O. Page that the American Minister to China will render appropriate assistance in Nanking regarding emergency communication facilities.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Secretary of State Stimson to F. O. Page regarding Emergency Communications in China
